titulo: A real routine and Jarvis up and running
lead: An assistant you don’t use is no use. In this lesson, you turn a weekly task into a standing request, use it five days in a row, and note what to improve. Then you see the steps to keep it running: on your computer, with automatic restarts, and on a rented server, up 24/7.
objetivo: use a standing request for five days in a row and choose where the assistant will run, from your laptop to a 24/7 server.

aprende.t: Turn a task into a standing request
The task list that gets you to step 3

hero_alt: Morning in soft light: a mug, an open planner, and a phone with a short list of three items.

secoes.sub: Four steps, from testing to 24/7. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: Where you finish lesson 4: green tests and a conversation in the terminal with the test model. No internet or key needed.
With the token and a real model, you can chat from your phone. Limit: when you close your laptop, the assistant goes to sleep too.

itens.t: Starts back up on its own

nos.detalhe: On Mac, the plan uses launchd: the assistant starts when you turn on your computer and restarts on its own if it stops. The logs stay in a folder for troubleshooting.

A rented server stays on day and night. The steps are the same: connect through the terminal, clone, and ask the agent to build it. The difference is packaging: for a server, the build page recommends Docker.

secoes.legenda: One at a time: Telegram, then automatic restart, then server. Move to each step only when the previous one is stable.

texto: Choose one of the three things it should do every week, from the plan in lesson 2.
Pick one thing you’d do anyway. That’s how you build a week of use.

exemplo.texto: Start the day with your top three priorities.

texto: Write the request in AGENTS.md: when you send a short word, it does the task the same way each time.
Scheduling it to run on its own (without you asking) is planned for the next phase. For now, you trigger it.

exemplo.texto: Every morning, when I send "day," list my top three priorities based on what I told you yesterday.

texto: Use it for five days in a row. Write one line each day: what worked and what was missing.
Got the tone wrong? SOUL. Forgot something? Memory. Did something it shouldn’t? AGENTS.

exemplo.texto: Day 3: listed 5 priorities instead of 3. Update AGENTS.

texto: Once a week, review your notes and the log, then change just one thing. Run the tests again.
There’s no ready-made assistant. There’s one that gets better with real use.

exemplo.texto: One change a week, with tests passing before and after.

secoes.sub: Copy these into your AGENTS.md and meu-jarvis.md.

blocos.conteudo:
## Standing requests
- When I send "day": list my top three priorities based on what I told you yesterday. No more than three, in short bullet points.
- When I send "end": ask what I finished today and save it to memory.

## Tasks I’d like to send and then go to bed
1.
2.
3.
4.
5.
(This list is the starting point for step 3: queues.)

abas.html:
You: day

Jarvis:

  1. Finish the sales report (it’s Monday).
  2. Reply to the client about the timeline.
  3. Prepare the agenda for Thursday’s meeting.

The three come from what you told it yesterday and from memory.

• Week 1: the core running on your main channel.
  • Week 2: memory really saving things and one or two tools.
  • Week 3: always on (automatic restart or a server).
  • Week 4: your first round of improvements based on the log and notes.

The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What makes a good standing request?
opcoes: "When I send 'day,' list my three priorities based on what I told you yesterday."
"Do what you think is best every morning."
perguntas.explica: There’s a trigger (the word), a task, a limit (three), and a source (what you told it). You can check whether it did the job right.

perguntas.p: You close your laptop, and the assistant stops responding. What fixes that?
opcoes: A rented server (VPS) that stays on 24 hours a day, using the same build process.
perguntas.explica: On your laptop, it sleeps when you do. On a server, it stays on day and night; Docker is the recommended way to package it for a server.

perguntas.p: On day 3, it listed five priorities instead of three. Where should you adjust that?
opcoes: In SOUL.md, by changing the personality.
In AGENTS.md, in the fixed request rule (no more than three).
perguntas.explica: It’s a work rule, so it belongs in AGENTS.md. Make one change, test again, and check the next day.

itens.texto: Channel, loop with a brake, identity, brain, memory, tools, and vault. Once you understand the pieces, you can choose better and make changes without fear.
SOUL, AGENTS, USER, and MEMORY are text. Change the text, and you change the assistant.
Brief + plan + request with tests. The test confirms it works; the promise doesn’t.
One owner, limits in the vault, one fixed request for a week, and one improvement at a time.
